newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola end sharply up on crushers, funds, CBOT.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola end sharply up on crushers, funds, CBOT.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended sharply higher on crusher demand and on sharp gains in CBOT soy complex futures linked to fund buying, traders said.

"We followed Chicago ahead of tomorrow's soybean ending stocks report," a trader said, referring to a USDA report to be released Tuesday, which is expected to show a cut in USDA's estimate of soybean ending stocks.

"Funds bought 400 to 700 May, crushers bought and the Pools sold," another trader said. May WCE futures crush profit margin rose to -3.60 Monday from -5.01 Friday. May-July spread at even money, May-Nov $51. Volume was 6,800 lots, or 136,000 tonnes, with 900 hedge lots.
Japan bought 8,000-10,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
March canola rose $9 to $425, May up $8.40 to $430.20.

Louis Dreyfus bought May flax up $2 to $361 with the Pools selling in active trade spurred by talk European crushers bought 5,000 tonnes, traders said. November closed up $3.30 at $328.50. Volume 500.

About 500 December wheat traded up $2.20 to $164.20 with locals, UGG, Alberta Wheat Pool and Louis Dreyfus trading, May rose $2.80 to $170.10 with RBC-DS buying. About 500 May-Dec spread at $5, 60 Mar-May $5. Oats didn't trade.

UGG sold March western barley up $2.80 to $143.70 to XCan, as RBC-DS covered March shorts and AWP and UGG sold May up $3.10 to $145.50 to PCTS with commission buy stops hit at $145, a trader said. July-Oct spread at $1.60. Volume was 1,500 lots.
UGG sold May feed peas up US$3.50 to US$210.50, RBC-DS sold July feed peas up the US$5/tonne limit to US$192.90, traders said.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas)
